title: Pass Play Integrity in 2 Minutes — Android 15 & 16 Trick

video_description:
If Google Play keeps telling you your device isn't certified, this is the fix — a few modules, one reboot, and the integrity checks come back green on Android 15 and Android 16.

You need root for this. KernelSU or Magisk, one of the two, already installed and working. From there it's a flash-and-run job: install the modules, reboot, then trigger each module's action in the right order. I filmed every tap so you can follow along without guessing which screen comes next.

🎯 What This Fixes
• Google Play Store showing "Device is certified" again.
• The basic, device and strong integrity verdicts passing.
• Apps that refuse to open on an unverified device.
• Works on Android 15 and Android 16 setups.

💡 The Order That Matters
1. Confirm KernelSU or Magisk is installed.
2. Flash the four modules from the all-files link, one at a time.
3. Reboot the phone.
4. Open KernelSU or Magisk and go to the modules section.
5. Run each module's action — the integrity command in Integrity Box, Play Integrity Fix, and check the Zygisk piece is active.
6. Re-check with the API checker; all three verdicts should now pass.
7. Open Play Store — if it errors at first, back out and reopen it, and it should show certified.
8. Check the bootloader state with Key Attestation.

❓ Common Questions
• Do I need root? Yes. The modules need KernelSU or Magisk to hook into the system.
• Which four modules? Integrity Box, Tricky Store, a Zygisk module, and Play Integrity Fix — the exact files are in the all-files link.
• Why did it fail the first time? Usually a missed reboot or the module actions not being run.
• Will it survive updates? Not forever — Google changes how it checks, so keep your modules updated.
• Does this work on both Android 15 and 16? Yes, both are covered here.

🚫 Where It Can Fail
• No root installed, so nothing can hook in.
• Skipping the reboot between flashing and running the module actions.
• Assuming it's permanent — these fixes need updating when Google moves the goalposts.
